column1: # Harnesses MEASURED to exceed a standard GitHub hosted runner (ubuntu-latest,
# 4 vCPU / 16 GB). The shard planner assigns these to shard 0, which no matrix leg
# selects: they are planned, counted against the census, and reported by the
# `Kani full census` job as **NOT RUN**. They are never counted as passes.
# This list is not a convenience. The failure mode is not a timeout — the runner VM
# dies and GitHub reports
#     ##[error]The runner has received a shutdown signal. This can happen when the
#     runner service is stopped, or a manually started runner is canceled.
# which is indistinguishable, from inside the job, from an infrastructure blip. A
# sweep that hits one of these is red for a reason nobody can attribute, and a
# permanently-red nightly is a nightly people learn to ignore. Naming them, with the
# run that killed the runner, keeps the sweep's green meaningful and keeps the gap
# visible instead of hiding it.
# Removing a name from this list is the right move as soon as either (a) the harness
# gets cheaper, or (b) the workflow moves to a larger runner. Raising the runner size
# is a repo-settings / billing change, not a workflow change: `runs-on:
# ubuntu-latest-8-cores` (or a self-hosted box) would very likely take all three.
# Until then these three are verified LOCALLY, one at a time, with the same command
# the workflow uses:
#   cargo kani --tests --features fuzz --jobs 1 --exact --harness <name>
# name\tevidence
